abstract.para: Snapshots do not differ in a technical sense. &snapper; distinguishes snapshots in two ways: by the event that triggers them and by how &snapper; handles them. The two classifications overlap. For example, installation snapshots are pre and post snapshots, and timeline snapshots are single snapshots.

section.title: Snapshot types by triggering event
section.para: &snapper; distinguishes the following types of snapshots, based on the events that trigger them. You can enable or disable two types independently.

listitem.para: Whenever you install, update or remove packages with zypper or with another tool based on libzypp, such as PackageKit (used, for example, by GNOME Software), a pair of snapshots is created: one before the system change (pre) and the other one after the system change (post). Old snapshots are automatically deleted. By default, up to ten important snapshots and up to ten regular ones are kept. Installation snapshots are enabled by default. To disable them, uninstall the package snapper-zypp-plugin.

Timeline snapshots are disabled for the root partition by default. When you enable them, &snapper; creates one snapshot every hour. The snapshots are created by the snapper-timeline.timer systemd timer. To change how often snapshots are created, modify this timer, as this cannot be configured within &snapper; itself.

The cleanup of timeline snapshots is based on hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly intervals. By default, &snapper; keeps the last ten hourly snapshots and the first snapshot of each of the last ten days, months and years. It deletes older snapshots automatically.

important.title: Exception for transactional systems
important.para: Installation snapshots do not apply to transactional systems. On these systems, each transactional-update run creates a new snapshot instead.

section.title: Snapshot types by time of creation
section.para: &snapper; recognizes three snapshot types by time of creation: pre, post and single. They do not differ physically, but &snapper; handles them differently.

listitem.para: A snapshot of a file system before a modification. Each pre snapshot corresponds to a post snapshot. For example, this is used for installation snapshots.
A snapshot of a file system after a modification. Each post snapshot corresponds to a pre snapshot. For example, this is used for installation snapshots.
A stand-alone snapshot. This is the default type when creating snapshots. For example, this is used for timeline snapshots.

section.para: This is an example list of snapshots after a fresh installation of a system and two subsequent software changes made through PackageKit:
section.screen: &prompt.sudo;snapper list # | Type | Pre # | Date | User | Used Space | Cleanup | Description | Userdata ---+--------+-------+----------------------------------+------+------------+---------+-----------------------+-------------- 0 | single | | | root | | | current | 1* | single | | Fri 02 Oct 2026 03:26:40 PM CEST | root | 180.88 MiB | | first root filesystem | 2 | pre | | Mon 05 Oct 2026 02:25:42 PM CEST | root | 689.28 MiB | number | zypp(packagekitd) | important=yes 3 | post | 2 | Mon 05 Oct 2026 02:28:19 PM CEST | root | 105.41 MiB | number | | important=yes 4 | pre | | Tue 10 Nov 2026 03:18:44 PM CET | root | 7.41 MiB | number | zypp(packagekitd) | important=yes 5 | post | 4 | Tue 10 Nov 2026 03:19:33 PM CET | root | 31.88 MiB | number | | important=yes
section.para: The asterisk (*) next to a snapshot number marks the snapshot that is currently mounted as the root file system. It is also the default snapshot to boot from.

Snapshot 0 with the description current is not a real snapshot. It always refers to the current state of the running system. The installer creates snapshot 1 with the description first root filesystem. It contains the initial installation of the system. In a post snapshot, the Pre # column shows the number of the matching pre snapshot
